newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel opens new front in fight for Thomson SA.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel opens new front in fight for Thomson SA.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom is prepared to make a new offer for state-owned electronics company Thomson SA if a rival bid by Lagardere, preferred by the government but now steeped in controversy, comes to nothing.

Chairman Serge Tchuruk told a parliament committee recently Alcatel could make a new bid and suggested the government could change strategy to sell Thomson off step-by-step while keeping it intact, minutes of his comments released on Tuesday show.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe's government has opted for a bid in which Lagardere would take over Thomson SA but hive off the consumer electronics unit Thomson Multimedia (TMM) to South Korean Daewoo Electronics.

But the plan, which still has to get clearance from France's privatisation commission, has sparked a bitter controversy among opposition politicians, trade unions, and staff who say the TMM sale to the Korean group for one franc defies economic logic.

Tchuruk told the National Assembly's finance committee in a closed-door hearing held last week that Alcatel could make a new offer which took account of the reactions to the Lagardere deal if the opportunity presented itself.
In the meantime, Alcatel was bound to its original offer, in which it envisaged keeping 50 percent of TMM, until the validity of that bid ran out on December 31.

"He (Tchuruk) made it known that, if the matter was still open beyond December 31 and given the interest of an alliance with the Thomson group, Alcatel Alsthom could envisage a new offer which would take account of developments in the meantime and the current reactions," the minutes from the hearing said.
An Alcatel spokesman, contacted by Reuters, confirmed the remarks as reported in the minutes.
"Among those reactions, the widening opposition to a pure and simple hiving off of Thomson Multimedia to a third party was understandable," the minutes reported Tchuruk as saying.

"Based on the idea of a return to better times, he (Tchuruk) indicated that a step-by-step privatisation of the capital of the entire Thomson group could ultimately prove more profitable for the state than the current procedure of a sale in one go," the minutes said.
Tchuruk highlighted that such a step could also address the issue of keeping Thomson intact.

Questioned on the jobs impact of an Alcatel offer, Tchuruk told the finance committee that restructuring of TMM could not be ruled out since the firm was suffering from having too many brands, but priority would be given to employment in France.
Juppe's government said last month it planned to sell the Thomson group to Lagardere for one franc after an injection of 11 billion francs ($2.1 billion).

Missiles-to-publishing group Lagardere plans to keep Thomson SA's 58 percent stake in profitable defence electronics group Thomson-CSF and sell the huge but loss-making TMM television set and video recorder manufacturer to Daewoo, again for one franc.
Tchuruk confirmed that his existing bid allowed for Alcatel to keep 50 percent of TMM and the handover to the government of any capital gains ultimately made by opening up TMM's capital.

Although the sale to Lagardere had initially looked like a done deal, the deeply unpopular Juppe has since made a gesture in the face of opposition and allowed for a parliament debate, although not a parliamentary vote on the issue.

Tchuruk, whose hopes of getting his hands on Thomson looked doomed a month ago when the government first announced that it had plumped for Lagardere and Daewoo, seemed to hold out hope of capitalising on the current controversy.
"The widening opposition to a pure and simple hiving off of Thomson Multimedia to a third party was understandable," the minutes of the hearing show Tchuruk as saying.
